items.title: Joe Lyde Interview, 1959-05-18
items.q: And he got Monty Sunshine, who in those days played his kind of steel clarinet

ctx.x: He came in 53. Uh-huh. 53. Yeah. Uh, stayed for a few months, I think. But Collier, Collier's always, Collier got his hands on some American music records, when he was in the Merchant Navy in the war, and brought them home and they decided that this was the real jazz and he got this bunch of fellas together. He had another cornet playing with him, uh, Sonny Morris. And he got Monty Sunshine, who in those days played his kind of steel clarinet that he'd seen a photograph of George Lewis playing, you know.
